newsitem.title: UK: UK air cargo industry plans new training course.
newsitem.headline: UK air cargo industry plans new training course.

text.p: The UK Air Freight Forum said it has agreed to cooperate on establishing an industry training scheme.

After a meeting held Tuesday, Andrew Traill of the British Shippers' Council (BSC), said this could lead to an air cargo industry-wide course sponsored by the Forum which comprises 20 major shippers, forwarders and airlines, said its members
"But first we must identify what is there," he said, referring to training programmes and courses already provided.
The Forum agreed a training module could be developed that would enable each group to understand the overall concept and logistics of the overall industry.

Mike Goodyear, intercontinental services manager of Forum member Royal Mail International, said a British International Freight Association (BIFA) training programme was a potential example for a training vehicle.
"What we are looking towards producing is an introduction to airfreight that would help airlines, forwarders and shippers," said Goodyear.
The BSC's Traill said that all new air cargo employees needed to have a broad-based knowledge of the industry.
"For example, a freight forwarding recruit must get to know about the airline side of the business and shippers' processes as well as his side of the industry," he noted.

"This industry will continue to suffer if it does not improve the calibre of the people in it and provides them with the depth and breadth of knowledge they need," said Traill. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+ 5017
